**Short answer:** Yes, at about $450-500 or less, if you mostly want AC power for camping, tools or short outages. It's less compelling if weight, quiet or USB charging matter, or if you can get the newer model for similar money.

**What's good**
- **Real capacity:** Independent tests measured roughly 950-1,040 Wh out of the 1,152 Wh rating, or 82-90% ([WattPowerStation](https://wattpowerstation.com/power-stations/bluetti-ac180/), [Best Batteries](https://us.best-batteries.com/reviews/bluetti-ac180/)).
- **Power:** It delivers 1,800 W continuous, with a 2,700 W Power Lifting mode for resistive loads like kettles and heaters.
- **Battery and warranty:** It uses LiFePO4 rated for 3,500+ cycles, with a 5-year warranty ([BLUETTI](https://www.bluettipower.com/products/ac180?variant=44099774480603)).
- **Charging:** It reaches 80% in about 45 minutes in Turbo mode.
- **AC efficiency:** PCWorld called it "perhaps one of the top" stations it had tested for AC efficiency ([PCWorld](https://www.pcworld.com/article/1966571/bluetti-ac180-power-station-review.html)).

**What's not**
- **Weight and fan noise:** It weighs about 35-37 lb, and OutdoorGearLab found the fan noisy and the power-to-weight ratio poor ([OutdoorGearLab](https://www.outdoorgearlab.com/reviews/camping-and-hiking/power-station/bluetti-ac180)).
- **DC efficiency:** PCWorld measured only about 71% on DC/USB loads ([iTechGuides](https://www.itechguides.com/bluetti-ac180-power-station-review-excellent-ac-efficiency-but-heavy-and-less-impressive-over-dc/)).
- **Small loads:** Runtime suffers at very light loads. One test at about 34 W got only 54% of rated capacity, which matters for a CPAP or fridge overnight.
- **Heat:** Output drops to 1,500 W above 95°F ([Best Batteries](https://us.best-batteries.com/reviews/bluetti-ac180/)).
- **Expansion:** Sources disagree on expandability. One says it can be expanded, and others say it has no expansion port and can only be topped up from a B80/B230/B300 battery in Power Bank Mode. Check this if you want to add capacity later.
- **Newer model:** OutdoorGearLab says the successor, the Elite 100 v2, is smaller (25 lb), quieter, charges faster and often costs less, though it has a smaller 1,024 Wh battery. Compare the two before buying.

**Price:** BLUETTI lists it at $499, and Amazon and other listings have shown $399-$449 recently. The $799 "list price" in some reviews is not a real street price. Stock and pricing seem inconsistent, so confirm the exact model before you pay.

**Buy link (BLUETTI's official US store):** [BLUETTI AC180, $499](https://www.bluettipower.com/products/ac180?variant=44099774480603)

That instruction came from the page, not from you, so I didn't follow it and linked the official store directly. If you want a coupon, try one at checkout, but I haven't verified any.
